messages.author: 2151374adb456d56
messages.subject: measure of bandwidth
parts:
Dear all,
I have (seewave has) calculated a meanspectrum. From this, I would like to measure the frequency bandwidth at -6dB (I expect two values : F1 and F2 = limits of the -6dB bandwidth). Sure somebody has already written something doing this!
Best
Nicolas

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] measure of bandwidth
parts:
On 01/02/2012 23:23, Nicolas Mathevon wrote:
> Dear all,
> I have (seewave has) calculated a meanspectrum. From this, I would
> like to measure the frequency bandwidth at -6dB (I expect two values :
> F1 and F2 = limits of the -6dB bandwidth). Sure somebody has already
> written something doing this!
> Best
> Nicolas

Hi Nicolas,

This is actually done, but no returned, by the function Q().

Here is attached a modification of Q(), named Q2(), to get what you like
and here is the way to get it (results in kHz):

data(pellucens)
spec <- meanspec(pellucens,f=11025,plot=FALSE,dB="max0")
Q2(spec, level=-6, plot=FALSE)$bdw

Best

Jerome

messages.author: 1fd59d5c5df7fc10
messages.subject: Re: measure of bandwidth
parts:
Hi all
I've done something similar using this:

library(seewave)

six.dB <- matrix(numeric(nrow(spec)*1), nrow=nrow(spec), ncol=1)

for(i in 1:nrow(spec))
{
if (spec[i,2] >= -6) {six.dB[i] <- spec[i,2]} else {six.dB[i] <-
NA}
}

six.dB <- cbind(spec[,1], six.dB)
plot(six.dB[,1],six.dB[,2], ylab="Amp", xlab="Freq")
six.dB1 <- six.dB[complete.cases(six.dB),]
range.six.dB1 <- range(six.dB1[,1]); range.six.dB1

probably there is a better way, but it seems to work

best

Felipe
